mainTopic: Past the allowed margin, is everything returned or only the excess? Three rejected proofs, then the משנה's case of a wine cellar with souring barrels
overview: Earlier, the גמרא brought רב הונא's rule that a buyer of produce must accept a small amount of dirt mixed in. It then asked: if there is more dirt than allowed, does the seller deduct all of it, or only the amount above the limit? The גמרא tries three proofs: the משנה about selling a בית כור of land, the laws of אונאה (overcharging), and a planter whose trees fail. Each one at first seems to show that past the limit, everything goes back. Each one is pushed away, because each case has a special reason of its own. Then the גמרא turns to the next case in the משנה, a buyer of a wine cellar who accepts ten souring barrels per hundred. It asks how the sale was worded and finds that a ברייתא fits neither option, so it adds the ten-percent rule to the ברייתא's general 'wine cellar' case. It defends this against רבי חייא's teaching about a single barrel. Then it is challenged again by רב זביד's ברייתא, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The land sale is different because the seller said 'more or less'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the בית כור משנה. There the seller explicitly allowed some leeway, and only a small extra was ever meant to be given up.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, in the land case, the seller told the buyer, 'whether it is less or more.' But a quarter is not significant, and more than a quarter is significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the attempted proof from the land-sale משנה. It says that case has a special reason of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the land case, the seller said up front 'less or more.' So he agreed to give up a small extra, up to a quarter-קב per בית סאה. Anything beyond that is significant, and he never agreed to give it up. So the land case says nothing about רב הונא's produce case, where the buyer simply expects some dirt.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that other case)
Whether less or more
A quarter (of a קב of land per בית סאה)
Significant, counts as something

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the land case rules against רב הונא. It is only saying the land case has its own reason, so it cannot be used as a proof either way.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, ״הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵיר״ אֲמַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: There, he said to him, 'whether less or more,'
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה about selling a בית כור of land, which the גמרא just tried to use as a proof.

phrases.english: but a quarter is not significant;
more than a quarter is significant,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵיר אֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for רב הונא's question that was brought just before this passage, from the בית כור משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the land-sale משנה as a model for רב הונא's produce case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The land case rests on the seller's stated 'less or more' and on extra land being significant. The produce case rests on the buyer's general expectation of dirt.

steps.title: Why more than a quarter counts as real land
steps.stepSummary: The extras from every בית סאה add up to a field big enough to plant nine קבין, so it is a real piece of land and must all be returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is fit to join together into an area of nine קבין, it becomes a significant piece of land on its own, and it goes back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why an extra of more than a quarter is called 'significant.' This finishes the rejection from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each small extra per בית סאה joins together across the whole field. Together they make a plot worth naming on its own. A real plot of land is not something the seller gives up, so all of it is returned.

keyTerms.meaning: To combine, join together
Nine קבין (an area planted with nine קב of seed)
On its own, in its own right

steps.whatToRemember: The land case is special: the seller said 'less or more,' and more than a quarter adds up to a real field. So it cannot prove what happens with dirt in produce.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֵיוָן דַּחֲזֵי לֵיהּ לְאִיצְטְרוֹפֵי בְּתִשְׁעַת קַבִּין,
phrases.english: for since it is fit to combine into nine קבין,
phrases.notes: A בית כור is thirty בית סאה, so the little extras from each one add up to a field you could plant nine קבין in.

phrases.aramaic: הָוְיָא לַהּ אַרְעָא חֲשִׁיבְתָּא בְּאַפֵּי נַפְשָׁא;
phrases.english: it becomes a significant piece of land on its own;
and it goes back.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכֵיוָן דַּחֲזֵי לֵיהּ לְאִיצְטְרוֹפֵי בְּתִשְׁעַת קַבִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word 'significant' from step 1 and closes the rejection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason behind the distinction
steps.terutzMaskana: Extra land beyond a quarter adds up to a real plot, so all of it is returned. That is a special reason that does not carry over to produce.

steps.title: A new proof from the laws of overcharging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about אונאה: less than a sixth, the sale stands; more than a sixth, the sale is cancelled; exactly a sixth, the sale stands and the overcharge is returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: about overcharging, if it is less than a sixth, the sale is final. If it is more than a sixth, the sale is cancelled. If it is exactly a sixth, the buyer acquires, and the overcharge is returned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to answer רב הונא's question. This step quotes the source, and the next steps explain the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of אונאה also have an 'allowed margin.' A small price gap is forgiven, and a big one is not. Exactly one-sixth is the in-between case, and there the whole overcharge is paid back.

keyTerms.meaning: Overcharging or underpaying, a price unfair to the market value
One-sixth
A purchase, a sale
Cancelled, void

phrases.english: Come and hear: Overcharging;
less than a sixth, the sale is acquired,
more than a sixth, the sale is cancelled.
Exactly a sixth, he acquires, and returns the overcharge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's question: past the limit, is everything deducted or only the excess?
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on אונאה and its rule for exactly one-sixth.

steps.title: Why not return just enough to get below a sixth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a puzzle in the ברייתא. At exactly a sixth, it would be enough to return a tiny bit and get under the limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let him return only until it is less than a sixth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a pointed question about the ברייתא to bring out the proof. It is setting up the conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Less than a sixth is forgiven. So at exactly a sixth, returning a tiny amount would bring the gap into the forgiven zone. Yet the ברייתא says he returns the whole overcharge, and that needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Let him return

phrases.english: Why? Let him return until less than a sixth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the 'exactly a sixth' line of the ברייתא from step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the whole overcharge is returned, and not just enough to get below one-sixth.

steps.title: Once you must return, you return everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that whenever something must be returned, the whole amount goes back. This supports רב הונא: all the dirt is deducted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: whenever one has to return, he returns all of it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the ברייתא, and it seems to answer רב הונא's question: past the limit, the whole amount is deducted. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא does not let the seller return just a little, the rule must be all or nothing. Once you cross the line, even the 'allowed' part goes back. So with produce, if there is too much dirt, the seller deducts all of it, not only the extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this
To return
All of it

steps.whatToRemember: This is the proof as the גמרא first offers it: once you pass the allowed margin, the whole amount goes back. Step 6 rejects this proof, so it does not settle רב הונא's question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the proof the גמרא is building toward. Notice exactly what it rests on, because step 6 will attack that point: whether the buyer agreed ahead of time to any margin at all.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, כׇּל הֵיכִי דְּבָעֵי לְאַהְדּוֹרֵי –
phrases.english: Learn from this: wherever he needs to return,
he returns all of it!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, כׇּל הֵיכִי דְּבָעֵי לְאַהְדּוֹרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 and completes the proof begun in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof concludes that once something must be returned for passing the allowed margin, the entire amount is returned. Step 6 rejects this proof.

steps.title: The overcharge case is different: the seller promised a fair price
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from אונאה. There the deal was 'fair value for fair value' from the start, so any noticeable overcharge must be fully returned. That tells us nothing about dirt, where the buyer expected some.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them?! There, the seller said from the start that it would be a fair price for fair value. It is just that less than a sixth is not noticed in a sale of a מנה, so people let it go. A sixth is noticed, and people do not let it go. More than a sixth makes it a mistaken sale, and the sale is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back the support it just found for רב הונא. It explains that the אונאה case works on a different basis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אונאה the buyer never agreed to any overcharge at all. Small amounts are only let go because nobody notices them, so once it is noticeable, all of it goes back. With dirt in produce, the buyer agreed ahead of time to accept a normal amount, so maybe only the part above that amount comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
Forgives, lets it go
A mistaken sale, which can be cancelled
A sum of one hundred זוז

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say רב הונא is wrong. It only says the אונאה ברייתא cannot prove him right.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, מֵעִיקָּרָא שָׁוֶה בְּשָׁוֶה אֲמַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: There, from the start he told him 'equal value for equal value,'
phrases.notes: 'There' means the overcharge case from step 3. The seller promised a fair price.

phrases.english: but less than a sixth
is not noticeable in a hundred, and a person lets it go;
a sixth is noticeable, and a person does not let it go;
more than a sixth is a mistaken sale,
and the sale is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support for רב הונא concluded in step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the אונאה ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In אונאה the buyer never agreed to any overcharge. In the dirt case the buyer agreed ahead of time to a normal amount.

steps.title: A new proof from a planter whose trees fail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a field owner accepts ten failed trees out of a hundred. If more fail, the planter must replace all of them. That looks like support for רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: when someone takes a field from his friend to plant trees in it, the owner accepts ten failed trees for every hundred. If more than that fail, all of them are placed on the planter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new source to support רב הונא. Here too there is an allowed amount, and going past it seems to make everything count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is just like the dirt case. There is a normal amount the owner expects and accepts. Yet once it goes past ten, the planter is responsible for all the failed trees, not just the extra ones.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes on a field to work it
Failed or barren trees
They roll it onto him, making him responsible

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who takes a field from his friend to plant trees —
this one accepts upon himself
ten failed trees for every hundred.
More than this —
they place all of it on him.
phrases.notes: The planter has to replace every failed tree, not just the ones past ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the אונאה proof was rejected, a new proof is brought
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's question: past the allowed amount, is everything deducted or only the excess?
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about failed trees in a planting deal

steps.title: Too many failed trees is like planting from scratch
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects the proof. When more than ten fail, the empty area adds up to a real field. So the planter is like someone just starting to plant, and he must do it all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: whenever it is more than this, it is like someone who comes to plant from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא rejects the tree proof. He explains that the tree case has its own reason for making everything count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Past ten failed trees, the bare spots together make up a full planting area. That is a new job of planting, not a small leftover. Dirt in produce never adds up to a separate unit like that, so this case does not prove רב הונא either.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who comes to plant from the beginning
Is similar to, is considered like

steps.whatToRemember: All three proofs about רב הונא's question (the land sale, the overcharge case and the trees case) were pushed back. Each has its own special reason for returning everything, so the question about dirt is not settled by them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Any time it is more than this,
it is like one who comes to plant from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the planting ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Past the limit, the failed trees make up a whole field to replant. Dirt never makes a separate unit like that.

steps.title: What kind of wine cellar sale does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a wine cellar and asks how the sale was worded. Did the seller say 'a wine cellar' in general, or 'this wine cellar'? Each option seems to cause a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'a cellar of wine,' etc. What is the case? If he said to him 'a wine cellar' without saying which, it is difficult. If he said to him 'this wine cellar,' it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section on the wine cellar case in the משנה. It sets up two possible readings and flags that both seem hard, getting ready to explain each problem next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a buyer of a wine cellar accepts ten sour barrels per hundred. The גמרא needs to know whether the sale was for wine in general or for this particular cellar. It says each option is 'difficult' but has not yet explained why. That comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A wine cellar
What is the case? What are the circumstances?
Without specifying
It is difficult

phrases.english: 'A cellar of wine,' etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting our משנה: a buyer of a wine cellar accepts ten sour barrels in a hundred.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he said to him:
'a wine cellar' without saying which — it is difficult;
if he said to him:
'this wine cellar' — it is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְתֵּף שֶׁל יַיִן וְכוּ׳. הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the dirt discussion to the next case in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the wine cellar sale was for wine in general or for a particular cellar, since each reading seems to cause a problem

steps.title: If the seller said 'this cellar,' a ברייתא contradicts the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Try the option where the seller pointed to one specific cellar. A ברייתא gives three wordings and three rulings, and none of them matches the משנה's rule of 'accept ten souring barrels per hundred.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'this cellar,' that is difficult. A ברייתא teaches: 'I am selling you a wine cellar' means he must give all good wine. 'I am selling you this wine cellar' means he may give ordinary shop-quality wine. 'I am selling you this cellar' means that even if it is all vinegar, the buyer gets what is there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the difficulties from step 9 by quoting a ברייתא. Its first case (all good wine for 'a wine cellar') clashes with the משנה on the general reading, and its other cases clash on the 'this cellar' reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three wordings. Each one has a clear result: all good wine, shop-quality wine, or whatever is in the cellar, even vinegar. Nowhere does it say 'accept ten souring per hundred,' so our משנה matches none of these wordings.

keyTerms.meaning: Cellar, where barrels of wine are stored
Wine of the kind sold in a shop: ordinary quality, which may be starting to turn
Vinegar, wine that has fully spoiled
It has come to him, meaning the buyer takes what is there

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the three wordings. 'A wine cellar' promises good wine. 'This wine cellar' promises wine from this cellar. 'This cellar' promises only the cellar's contents. The more specific the seller is, the less he promises about quality.

phrases.english: If he said to him, 'this cellar,' it is difficult,
for it was taught: 'A cellar of wine
I am selling to you':
he gives him wine that is all good.
'This cellar of wine
I am selling to you':
he gives him wine of the kind sold in a shop.
'This cellar I am selling to you':
even if it is all vinegar, it has come to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: ״מַרְתֵּף זֶה״ – קַשְׁיָא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works through the second option raised in step 9's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both readings of the משנה from step 9: a general 'wine cellar' sale and a sale of 'this wine cellar'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives a different ruling for every wording, and none of them is the משנה's ten-per-hundred rule.

steps.title: The משנה means 'a wine cellar,' and the ten-percent rule is added to the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about a seller who said 'a wine cellar' without details. The ברייתא's first case should include the rule that the buyer accepts ten souring barrels per hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he said 'a wine cellar' without specifying which one. Add to the first part of the ברייתא: and the buyer accepts ten souring barrels per hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is about a general 'wine cellar' sale. It adjusts the ברייתא's first case so that it matches the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'all good wine' for a general sale. The גמרא now reads that case as also allowing up to ten souring barrels per hundred. That way the ברייתא and the משנה say the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact: the גמרא is going back to an option it set aside
Without details, in general terms
The first part of a teaching
Barrels of wine that are starting to sour

phrases.english: Really, it is where he said to him
'a cellar of wine,' without specifying,
and teach in the first part of the ברייתא:
and he accepts upon himself
ten souring barrels per hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by switching to the general-sale option and adjusting the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing which case is meant, plus adding words to the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'all good wine' meant not even one souring barrel.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a general 'wine cellar' sale the wine should be good, but the buyer accepts up to ten souring barrels per hundred.

steps.title: רבי חייא says a sold barrel must be all good wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the fix: in a general sale, does the buyer accept any bad wine? רבי חייא taught that someone who sells a barrel must give wine that is all good.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a general sale, does the buyer accept bad wine? But רבי חייא taught: one who sells a barrel of wine to his friend must give him wine that is all good!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 11. A general sale seems to require completely good wine, with no allowance for souring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said a general sale allows ten souring barrels per hundred. רבי חייא's teaching about a barrel sold without details demands all good wine. The two seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel, here a barrel of wine
But it was taught: this introduces a source that seems to contradict

phrases.english: But in a sale without specifying, does he accept?!
But רבי חייא taught:
one who sells a barrel of wine to his fellow
gives him wine that is all good!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a general sale allows ten souring barrels per hundred
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא requires all good wine in a sale without details, which leaves no room for any souring.

steps.title: A single barrel is different
steps.stepSummary: A barrel holds one batch of wine, so the whole thing must be good. A cellar holds many separate barrels, so a few bad ones are expected.
steps.simpleTranslation: A barrel is different, because it is all one wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from רבי חייא by showing that his case is different from a cellar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside one barrel, all the wine is the same, so it is either good or bad, and the buyer expects good. A cellar has many barrels that age differently, so some souring among them is normal. רבי חייא's ruling therefore does not apply to a cellar.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Wine (Aramaic)

phrases.english: A barrel is different,
because it is all one wine.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any general wine sale requires all good wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a single barrel, which holds one batch of wine, must be completely good. A cellar of many barrels allows some souring.

steps.title: רב זביד's ברייתא puts the ten-percent rule on 'this wine cellar'
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא, from the school of רבי אושעיא, says 'a wine cellar' means all good wine. It applies the ten-souring-per-hundred rule to 'this wine cellar' instead. That contradicts the answer from step 11.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב זביד taught a ברייתא from the school of רבי אושעיא: 'I am selling you a wine cellar' means he gives all good wine. 'I am selling you this wine cellar' means he gives all good wine, and the buyer accepts ten souring barrels per hundred...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that puts the ten-percent rule on the specific wording 'this wine cellar,' not on a general sale. The ברייתא continues past this point, and the גמרא's answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the ten-percent rule belongs to the general 'a wine cellar' case. רב זביד's version gives the general case all good wine with no allowance. It puts the ten-per-hundred rule on 'this wine cellar,' so the fix from step 11 looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: From the school (study hall) of רבי אושעיא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two ברייתות. The first one (step 10) gave 'this wine cellar' shop-quality wine. רב זביד's version gives that same wording all good wine with ten-percent souring allowed.

phrases.english: But didn't רב זביד teach
from the school of רבי אושעיא:
'A cellar of wine I am selling to you':
he gives him wine that is all good.

phrases.aramaic: ״מַרְתֵּף זֶה שֶׁל יַיִן אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ״ –
phrases.english: 'This cellar of wine I am selling to you':
he gives him wine that is all good,
and he accepts upon himself ten souring barrels per hundred,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תָּנֵי רַב זְבִיד דְּבֵי רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 13 defended the answer from step 11, this brings a new challenge against that answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 11's placement of the ten-percent rule in the general 'a wine cellar' case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב זביד's ברייתא gives the general case all good wine and puts the ten-percent rule on 'this wine cellar.'
